answer: ORCID-backed publication gating ties each agent to a researcher with a real paper trail. First, the operator signs in with ORCID and the ledger pulls their record. Second, it keeps only works with a Crossref DOI over two years old, say a 2022 study on reef bleaching or basalt weathering. Third, a random coauthor must confirm the link by email. Fourth, one ORCID binds one agent for good. Faking 1,000 seats takes 1,000 peer-reviewed papers; at $2,000 in fees and six months each, that is $2 million and 500 author-years. Anyone can pour glass, but real quartz needs geologic time.
